raw_text:
Below is a 12-week, upper-body–focused program designed for a recreational climber with a history of right subacromial impingement. It respects the current constraint: pain-free range only and no overhead loading. It emphasizes scapular control, posterior-chain dominance, horizontal pulling/pushing in safe ranges, gradual return to climbing-specific demands, and balanced lower-body/core so she stays robust overall. It’s organized into 3 phases with progressive exposure, clear exercise selections, sets/reps, tempo, and weekly structure. Include ongoing pain monitoring: 0–2/10 acceptable during exercise that resolves within 24 hours and does not produce next-day increase; otherwise regress load/range.

Global structure
- Frequency: 3 upper-body–focused sessions per week (e.g., Mon/Wed/Fri), plus 1–2 lower-body/core accessory sessions or add-ons where noted. Optional easy aerobic work 2x/week for recovery.
- Overhead restriction: No vertical pressing or loaded overhead positions. Scapular elevation work is isometric/dynamic below painful arc only. Keep shoulder flexion/abduction below symptom threshold; typically work in 0–120° flexion if pain-free, but honor her range.
- Climbing: Light, technique-only traversing introduced in Phase 2 if pain-free and cleared by physio; no dynos, lock-offs, gastons, or high reaches. Emphasize footwork and hips.
- Warm-up each session (8–12 min): 
  - 3–4 min light cardio
  - Thoracic mobility (open books, thread the needle), gentle scapular clocks, neck/first-rib resets as tolerated
  - Activation: low-load serratus (supine punch plus, wall slides in pain-free arc), lower traps (prone Y/partial range), rotator cuff isometrics, banded scap retraction/protraction
- Tempo notation example: 3-1-1 = lower 3s, pause 1s, lift 1s. Rest 60–90s for accessories, 90–150s for compounds.

Phase overview
- Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Calm tissue, build capacity. Emphasis on scapular control, cuff endurance, horizontal pulling bias, pain-free pressing arcs (neutral grip), tempo control, isometrics. No climbing yet.
- Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Increase load and range within tolerance, add more unilateral work, integrate climbing-specific patterns (isometric holds, controlled eccentrics), introduce light, technique-only traversing if symptom-free.
- Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Strength and capacity building. Heavier horizontal pulling/pushing, power-endurance elements (submax repeats), more advanced scapular loading, cautious return to climb-specific intervals. Still no overhead loading.

Exercise key themes (used throughout)
- Scapular mechanics: serratus anterior (push-up plus, wall slides), lower trap (prone or incline raises partial range), mid trap/rhomboids (rows with scapular retraction/depression).
- Rotator cuff: isometrics early; short/long-lever external rotation with towel roll; eccentric bias later.
- Push patterns: neutral-grip DB press, push-ups to elevation, landmine press is typically overhead-ish so avoid; cable press at ~30–60° abduction if pain-free.
- Pull patterns: chest-supported rows, 1-arm cable rows, low-to-mid-angle pulldowns with neutral grip staying below shoulder level; avoid end-range overhead hang.
- Forearm/grip: extensor/flexor endurance, pronation/supination; open-hand grip focus (climber-safe).
- Core/hip: anti-rotation/anti-extension, posterior chain.

Progression and pain rules
- Progress 2–5% load or 1–2 reps weekly if all sets at RPE 6–7 and no next-day irritation.
- If pain appears, first reduce ROM, then tempo slower, then load; swap to isometric variant if needed.

Week-by-week plan

Phase 1: Foundation and symptom control (Weeks 1–4)
Goal: Normalize scapulohumeral rhythm, improve cuff endurance and serratus/lower trap activation, establish pain-free pressing/pulling arcs. Emphasize tempo, isometrics, neutral grips.

Weekly schedule template
- Session A (Horizontal Pull Emphasis)
- Session B (Horizontal Push + Scap Control)
- Session C (Unilateral Pull/Push + Cuff/Grip)
- Optional lower-body/core finisher 1–2x/week (brief)

Week 1
Session A
- Chest-supported DB row (neutral grip), 3x12, 3-1-1, RPE 6
- 1-arm cable row (elbow near torso, slight torso rotation allowed), 3x10/side, 2-1-2
- Scapular push-up (protraction/retraction, small ROM), 3x12, 2-2-2
- Supine serratus punch (DB light), 3x15, 2-1-2
- ER isometric at 30° abduction with towel roll (band), 3x20–30s/side
- Wrist extensor eccentrics (DB), 3x12/side, 3-1-1
Finisher: Farmer carry (suitcase, opposite hand heavier if asymmetry), 3x30–40m each, upright, ribs down

Session B
- Neutral-grip DB floor press (pain-free range), 4x8, 3-1-1, RPE 6
- Cable chest press from split stance, handle height just below shoulder, 3x10/side
- Prone incline T raise (thumbs up), partial range, 3x12, 2-1-2
- Wall slide with lift-off only if pain-free (limit range), 3x8, slow
- IR isometric at 30° abduction, 3x20–30s/side
- Dead bug or hollow hold (pain-free), 3x20–30s

Session C
- Seated low row (neutral grip), 4x10, 2-1-2
- Push-up to elevated surface (bench/wall), 4x8, 3-1-1
- 1/2-kneeling cable face pull to chest height (avoid end-range elevation), 3x12
- Side-lying ER with towel roll, 3x15, 2-1-2
- Scapular depression holds on dip bars (no shoulder extension beyond neutral), 3x20–30s
- Forearm pronation/supination (hammer), 2x12 each

Week 2
- Keep structure, add 1 rep per set where pain-free or +2–5% load.
- Add tempo pause in retracted position on rows (1s).
- Introduce isometric mid-range DB press hold (neutral grip) at the top of floor press, 3x15–20s in last set.

Week 3
- Progress to 4 sets on primary rows/presses.
- Add cable low trap raise (bilateral, arms ~30–60° flexion), 3x10 slow.
- Push-up elevation slightly lower if pain-free (maintain RPE 6–7).
- Introduce banded ER to 45° abduction (short lever), 2x15 light.

Week 4
- Mild deload volume (-20–25%) but maintain intensity: 3 sets on compounds, hold loads.
- Quality focus: scapular upward rotation without shrug; confirm zero next-day irritation.
- Add light isometric “hang” on rings at 90° elbow flexion (feet assisted), scapula set, 3x20s if pain-free.

Phase 2: Capacity and controlled range expansion (Weeks 5–8)
Goal: Increase loads and reps in pain-free range, integrate unilateral bias, introduce slow eccentrics for cuff, add gentle climbing-specific work (if symptom-free). Start technique-only traversing 1x/week (10–20 min, big holds, hips/feet-driven, no hard reaches), stop if any pain.

Weekly template remains A/B/C with added climbing tech session on an easy day.

Week 5
Session A (Pull bias)
- Chest-supported row (heavier), 4x8, 2-1-1, RPE 7
- 1-arm cable row with slight reach at stretch then retract, 3x10/side
- Low-angle neutral-grip pulldown, stop before painful arc, 3x10, 3-1-1
- Serratus push-up plus (knees if needed), 3x12–15
- ER eccentric at 0–30° abduction (band or cable), 3x8/side, 4-0-1
- Wrist roller (extension focus), 2–3 runs

Session B (Push/scap)
- Neutral-grip DB bench (flat or slight incline ≤15°, verify pain-free), 4x8, 3-1-1
- Cable fly low-to-mid arc (palms neutral), short range, 3x12 light
- Prone incline Y raise partial, 3x10, 3-1-1
- Cable face pull to external rotation only if pain-free (limit elevation), 3x12
- IR eccentric (band/cable), 3x8/side, 4-0-1
- Pallof press, 3x12/side

Session C (Unilateral + grip)
- 1-arm chest-supported row (off bench), 3x10/side
- Push-up to lower box, 4x8–10
- Cable press from half-kneel (contralateral stance), 3x10/side
- Scap depression holds, 3x25–30s
- Finger extensor bands, 3x20; rice bucket or putty 2–3 min
- Carry: offset front rack (light KB) on left/right, 3x20–30m/side

Week 6
- Progress loads/reps where RPE ≤7. Add 1 set to primary presses/rows if no symptoms (5 sets total on one main lift per session).
- Add ring rows with feet supported, neutral grip, 3x8–10 within pain-free range.
- Climbing technique: 2 short bouts of 6–8 min traversing, easy terrain, 2–3 min rest, stop if shoulder discomfort.

Week 7
- Introduce cluster sets on rows for quality: e.g., chest-supported row 3x(4+4) with 20s intra-set rest, RPE 7.
- Add push-up eccentric emphasis: 3s down, light assist up, 3x8 if needed.
- Add cable external rotation at 45–60° abduction short range, 3x12 light if tolerated.
- Climbing tech: add easy downclimb ladders on big holds below shoulder height, 10–12 min total.

Week 8
- Deload volume 20–25%, keep intensity. Maintain light climbing technique if totally symptom-free. Reassess ROM and tolerated arcs. Re-emphasize mobility and tissue quality.

Phase 3: Strength and climbing-capacity emphasis without overhead loading (Weeks 9–12)
Goal: Build stronger horizontal press/pull, scapular endurance/power-endurance, integrate controlled repeat-effort sets that mimic climbing time-under-tension while respecting no-overhead rule. Expand traversing volume slightly if pain-free.

Week 9
Session A (Pull strength)
- Chest-supported row heavy, 5x5, 2-1-1, RPE 7–8
- 1-arm cable row, 4x8/side
- Neutral-grip low pulldown, 4x8
- Serratus push-up plus, 3x15
- ER at 45–60° abduction, 3x10, slow
- Carry: heavy suitcase, 4x30–40m/side

Session B (Press strength/control)
- Neutral-grip DB bench, 5x5, RPE 7–8
- Push-up to moderate box, 4x8–10 (2-1-1)
- Cable press (half-kneel), 3x10/side, slight forward reach at end if painless
- Prone Y/T combo (partial), 3x10 each
- IR eccentric, 3x8/side, 4-0-1
- Anti-rotation press walkouts, 3x6 steps/side

Session C (Capacity + cuff)
- Ring rows feet forward (adjust difficulty), 4x10
- Dumbbell floor press with 2s pause at bottom, 4x8
- Face pull to chest (avoid high elevation), 3x12–15
- Scap depression/retraction holds on cable (straight arms to hip), 3x12 with 2s hold
- Forearm complex: pron/sup + ext eccentrics, 2 rounds
Climbing tech: 2–3 bouts of 8–10 min easy traversing with long rests; no high reaches.

Week 10
- Progress loads (+2–5%) on 5x5 lifts if RPE ≤8.
- Introduce repeat-effort sets for endurance:
  - Row repeaters: chest-supported row 3x12 with 30s rest between mini-sets of 6+6.
  - Push repeaters: elevated push-ups 3xAMRAP sets to RPE 8, cap at technical failure.
- Add band-assisted scapular protraction/retraction in tall plank (knees if needed), 3x8–10.

Week 11
- Strength top-up:
  - DB bench 4x6 heavy, last set + drop set 1x10 light.
  - Chest-supported row 4x6 heavy, last set + 1x12 back-off.
- Introduce horizontal “lock-off” isometrics at safe angles:
  - 1-arm cable row hold at 90° elbow, scap set, 3x15–20s/side, moderate load.
  - Push isometric: cable press hold mid-range, 3x15–20s/side.
- Climbing: maintain easy-tech volume; add footwork drills; still avoid any overhead reach or powerful moves.

Week 12 (Consolidate and test tolerance)
- Reduce volume 20%, keep intensity moderate-high to consolidate.
- Optional tolerance checks (pain-free only):
  - Neutral-grip DB bench 3x5 @ prior week’s load.
  - Chest-supported row 3x5 @ prior week’s load.
- Capacity finisher circuit (2 rounds, low pain risk):
  - Ring rows 12
  - Elevated push-ups 10
  - Scap pull-down to hips (straight-arm depression) 12
  - Serratus wall slide small range 8
  Rest 60–90s between moves.

Lower-body/core add-ons (1–2x/week, 20–30 min)
- Hip hinge: RDL or trap-bar deadlift 3–4x6–8
- Split squat or step-up 3x8–10/side
- Hamstring curls/glute bridge 3x12
- Core: side plank, dead bug variations, Pallof presses
Keep upper traps relaxed, avoid heavy front-rack if it aggravates shoulder.

Recovery, mobility, and monitoring
- Daily micro-dose (5–8 min): thoracic open books, cat-cow, gentle scap clocks, supine breathing with reach (serratus), neck/pec minor soft tissue (gentle).
- Post-session: light forearm/hand tissue work, pec and posterior cuff stretches only in pain-free range.
- Sleep: 7–9 hours; avoid sleeping with arm overhead.
- Pain-log: note exercises, side, intensity, and next-day response. Adjust by reducing range, tempo slower, or swapping to isometric if pain >2/10 or lingers >24h.

Nutrition basics to support tissue capacity
- Protein: ~1.6–2.2 g/kg/day spread over 3–5 meals; include 20–30 g high-quality protein within 2 hours post-training.
- Overall calories: at least maintenance to support tendon adaptation; small surplus (+5–10%) if recovery is lagging.
- Hydration: 30–40 ml/kg/day; add electrolytes for sessions >60 min.
- Omega-3s and collagen/gelatin option: 10–15 g gelatin or 15–20 g collagen + 50–100 mg vitamin C 30–60 min pre-session may support tendon; optional.

Return-to-sport guidance
- Continue avoiding overhead loading until explicitly cleared by her physio.
- If phases progress without symptoms, maintain Phase 3 structure beyond Week 12 while gradually increasing climbing technique volume and difficulty, still prioritizing footwork and hips.
- Before introducing overhead or dynamic climbing moves, ensure:
  - Pain-free full daily activities
  - Horizontal press 0.75x bodyweight (DB or barbell equivalent) and strong, pain-free rows
  - External rotation strength symmetry within ~10–15% and no apprehension in elevated positions (assessed by physio)

This plan keeps her climbing identity supported while building the scapular/cuff foundation, horizontal strength, and endurance she needs, without violating the no-overhead constraint. Adjust loads and ranges based on her daily symptom response and physio feedback.
